newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt, Israel killed POWs in 1956 - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Israel killed POWs in 1956 - newspaper.

text.p: An Israeli inquiry has concluded that Egyptian and Israeli troops both killed prisoners of war during the Suez crisis 40 years ago, Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth reported on Thursday.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received the draft report a few weeks ago but judged it too politically explosive to publicise at a time of tense relations with Egypt, Israel's peace partner since 1979, the daily said.
"The committee discovered one instance in which Israeli soldiers were involved in the killing of Egyptian prisoners of war," the paper said.
The inquiry also found "a series of incidents" in which Egyptian soldiers killed Israeli POWs, Yedioth Ahronoth added but gave no further details on either side.
Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak could not be reached for comment on the newspaper report but the story quoted his reaction as having been: "When we decide to publish the report, we'll announce it."
Charges of war crimes surfaced last year when a retired Israeli army officer told a newspaper of the killing of 49 Egyptian prisoners of war during the 1956 Israeli drive across the Sinai desert.
An Israeli military historian said days later his research showed Israeli troops killed 300 Egyptian prisoners in the 1967 Middle East war. Israel said soldiers on both sides committed atrocities.
The newspaper said the committee turned up no evidence of war crimes in other unspecified allegations it examined.

Eight months ago, then-Prime Minister Shimon Peres appointed an army reserve general to investigate the charges. Tensions with Egypt have since risen with the slowing of peace moves under right-winger Netanyahu, who ousted Peres in May.

Israeli forces swept into the Egyptian Sinai in October 1956 following a secret agreement with Britain and France for joint military action to regain control of the Suez Canal, nationalised by then-Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser.
